extracted.intended_audience: editors, collectors, and scholars of traditional/folk ballads (folklorists, literary historians)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing, annotating, and publishing editions of traditional (here Scottish) ballads: collating oral copies and printed variants, supplying glosses, historical context, and—where available—musical notation and comparative commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish from collation of multiple recited copies
rubrics_metrics.description: “This ballad is published from the collation of two copies, obtained from recitation.” Use collation of oral recitations as the basis for text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect multiple orally transmitted versions and collate them to reconstruct the best available text; state how many copies were collated and that they were taken from recitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare variants and related works to judge derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether a piece is the rude original, a corrupted copy, or derived from another (e.g., “It seems to be the rude original, or perhaps a corrupted and imperfect copy, of The Child of Elle”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare similar ballads and literary sources to assess relationships, derivation, and possible corruption; explicitly state hypotheses about dependence or common origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge translations, adaptations, and editorial influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Note when later authors translated or imitated a ballad without acknowledgment (example: Bürger's unacknowledged imitation of The Child of Elle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State when versions/poems are translations or imitations, and point out unacknowledged borrowings; when editorial corrections or emendations have been made, record and justify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate modernizations and degree of 'currency' in language
rubrics_metrics.description: When language has been modernized or corrected in transmission, note that fact (e.g., “much of the language seems somewhat modernized”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark any modernization or modernization extent; distinguish between ancient language and modernized renderings and explain editorial choices about retaining or altering wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide glosses/footnotes for archaic words and dialect
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply explanatory footnotes for obscure or dialect terms (examples: footnotes for 'sained', 'bale', 'eiry', 'erlish', 'esk', 'coft').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate difficult vocabulary, local idioms, and archaisms with clear glosses so readers understand the original terms and their senses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give provenance, locality, and historical context (but be cautious)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report local tradition and specific localizing details (e.g., sites, towers, stones, historical personages) while acknowledging uncertainty about origins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record claims of locality and connecting historic figures or places; supply documentary or topographic evidence where possible and note when local tradition may be speculative or prone to later accretions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warn about corruptions in cheap printed forms (penny pamphlets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed penny pamphlets frequently produce corrupt readings and ridiculous errors (example given: 'blue gilded horn' for 'bugelet horn').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer orally recorded versions or well-collated manuscripts over cheap printings; when using printed broadsides, point out obvious corruptions and correct them or explain emendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include musical notation and source citations when available
rubrics_metrics.description: When a melody exists in print or manuscript, include the music and cite the source (example: The Three Ravens given with music adapted to four voices from Ravencroft's Metismata, 1611).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide musical setting/notation and performance notes where extant; cite source editions and adaptations (date, title) and indicate voice arrangements or performance practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record editorial omissions or editorializing choices
rubrics_metrics.description: If burdens, refrains, or repetitions are omitted in reproduction, state the omission (example: omitted only the burden and repetition of the first line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about any material left out of a reproduction (refrain, burdens, repeated lines), and explain editorial rationale for omission or alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain cultural background, motifs, and superstitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide interpretive notes on cultural practices and superstitions invoked by the ballad (example: the lykewake, beliefs about leaving doors ajar, ceremonies to make the dead speak).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give ethnographic or folkloric explanations of motifs and rituals present in the text so readers understand social and belief contexts that inform the ballad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative literary parallels to illustrate themes and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare verses with lines from other romances or poems to show common motifs or stylistic touchstones (examples: compare a verse with an old romance or Bürger's translation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and quote parallel passages from related literature to illuminate imagery, emotive effects, or common poetic strategies; use such comparisons to argue for chronology or influence when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate which stanzas/verses derive from which sources
rubrics_metrics.description: When parts of the text are taken from different sources (oral vs printed), indicate source provenance for specific verses (example: 'The three last verses are given from the printed copy, and from tradition').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate the text to show variant provenance at the stanza/line level so readers can trace which lines derive from which witness and understand editorial conflation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess antiquity and currency with corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate claims of a ballad's antiquity or long currency (example: Hogg's conviction of antiquity despite some modernized language; ability to 'trace it back several generations').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions about age and oral currency with genealogies of transmission, citations of informants, manuscript or print witnesses, and local testimony; be transparent about certainty levels.
